**Common proteins that reside in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical proteins (examples) | Function | |----------|-----------------------------|----------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** – pumps Na⁺ out and K⁺ in
• **Aquaporins (e.g., AQP1, AQP4)** – water channels
• **Glucose transporters (GLUT1, GLUT4)** – facilitate glucose uptake
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ion channels** – voltage‑gated Na⁺, K⁺, Ca²⁺ channels; ligand‑gated channels (e.g., nicotinic acetylcholine receptor)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** – e.g., EGFR, HER2
• **Integrins** – mediate cell‑matrix adhesion
• **Cadherins** – mediate cell‑cell adhesion (e.g., E‑cadherin) | Transport, signaling, adhesion, ion homeostasis | | **Peripheral (non‑integral) proteins** | • **Annexins** – bind phospholipids in a Ca²⁺‑dependent manner
• **Glycophorins** – major hemoglobin‑binding proteins on erythrocytes
• **Scaffold proteins** – e.g., PSD‑95 in neurons | Modulate membrane structure, signaling complexes | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | • **GPI‑anchored proteins** – e.g., CD59, prion protein (PrPC)
• **S‑prenylated proteins** – e.g., Ras family GTPases | Signal transduction, membrane anchoring | | **Transporters & channels (secondary active transport)** | • **Sodium‑glucose linked transporter (SGLT1)**
• **Chloride channels (ClC family)** | Coupled transport of ions/substances | | **Other functional proteins** | • **Enzymes** – e.g., alkaline phosphatase, ecto‑nucleotidases
• **Antigen‑presenting molecules** – MHC class I & II
• **Co‑receptors** – CD4, CD8 on T cells | Immune recognition, enzymatic activity | > **Note:** > * The plasma membrane contains thousands of distinct proteins; the table above lists only a few of the most widely studied and functionally important examples. > * Many proteins belong to families (e.g., the GPCR superfamily has ~800 members in humans). > * The exact composition varies between cell types and physiological conditions.
